claim: Computer models of the human ventricular cardiomyocyte action potential have reached a level of detail and maturity that has led to an increasing number of applications in the pharmaceutical sector.
source: Computer models of the human ventricular cardiomyocyte action potential (AP) have reached a level of detail and maturity that has led to an increasing number of applications in the pharmaceutical sector.
evidence: This is a general statement about the state of the field, drawing from established scientific consensus about model development and applications.

claim: The most updated cardiomyocyte models include fine representations of ion movements through various important channels, pumps, and exchangers.
source: The most updated models include fine representations of ion movements through various important channels, pumps, and exchangers, and take the complex handling of intracellular calcium accurately into account (Grandi et al., 2010; O'Hara et al., 2011; Tomek et al., 2019; Bartolucci et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to published models.

claim: The most updated cardiomyocyte models take the complex handling of intracellular calcium accurately into account.
source: The most updated models include fine representations of ion movements through various important channels, pumps, and exchangers, and take the complex handling of intracellular calcium accurately into account (Grandi et al., 2010; O'Hara et al., 2011; Tomek et al., 2019; Bartolucci et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to published models.

claim: Cardiomyocyte models have individual strengths and limitations in replicating different aspects of physiology, pathology, and pharmacology.
source: While these models have individual strengths and limitations in replicating different aspects of physiology, pathology, and pharmacology (Corrado et al., 2021; Amuzescu et al., 2021), their degree of credibility has reached a level that has led to an increasing number of applications in academia and beyond.
evidence: Supported by citations to comparative studies.

claim: The Comprehensive in Vitro Proarrhythmia Assay (CiPA) was proposed in 2013 following a workshop at the US Food and Drug Administration.
source: To improve the regulatory assessment of a drug's proarrhythmic potential, the Comprehensive in Vitro Proarrhythmia Assay (CiPA) was proposed in 2013 following a workshop at the US Food and Drug Administration (Sager et al., 2014; Colatsky et al., 2016; Strauss et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to CiPA initiative publications.

claim: A central component of CiPA is a computer model of human ventricular cardiomyocyte electrophysiology coupled to a pharmacological model.
source: A central component is a computer model of human ventricular cardiomyocyte EP that is coupled to a pharmacological model describing the interaction between a given drug and multiple arrhythmia-relevant channels (Dutta et al., 2017; Li et al., 2017; Li et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to CiPA methodology papers.

claim: Bottino et al., 2006 estimated pharmacological parameters from action potentials of canine Purkinje fibers.
source: Some relevant examples for the latter have been presented by Bottino et al., 2006 who estimated pharmacological parameters from APs of canine Purkinje fibers and by Tveito et al. who estimated pharmacological parameters from AP biomarkers measured in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (Tveito et al., 2018) and several animal ventricular cardiomyocytes (Tveito et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Bottino et al., 2006.

claim: Tveito et al. estimated pharmacological parameters from AP biomarkers measured in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes.
source: Some relevant examples for the latter have been presented by Bottino et al., 2006 who estimated pharmacological parameters from APs of canine Purkinje fibers and by Tveito et al. who estimated pharmacological parameters from AP biomarkers measured in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (Tveito et al., 2018) and several animal ventricular cardiomyocytes (Tveito et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Tveito et al., 2018.

claim: Uncertainty in experimental data results from beat-to-beat variability, cell-to-cell variability, and measurement errors.
source: When the models are interfaced with experimental data, attention should be paid to the inherent uncertainty in the data that results from beat-to-beat variability (intrinsic variability), cell-to-cell variability (extrinsic variability), and measurement errors (observational uncertainty) (Mirams et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Mirams et al., 2016.

claim: Gaussian process emulators are not well suited to capture discontinuities of the response surface.
source: However, GP emulators are not well suited to capture discontinuities of the response surface as standard GP emulators assume a smooth and continuous response to changes in parameter values.
evidence: Based on established knowledge about Gaussian process properties.

claim: Neural networks can approximate even discontinuous functions with arbitrary precision in theory.
source: In contrast, it has been proven that neural networks (NN) can approximate even discontinuous functions with arbitrary precision in theory (Hornik et al., 1989), while recent works using NNs show empirically promising results for modeling partial differential equations containing discontinuities (Jagtap et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hornik et al., 1989.

claim: The ToR-ORd-dynCl simulator was used as the simulator in this study.
source: The simulator of Tomek et al., 2020 (ToR-ORd-dynCl simulator) was used.
evidence: Direct statement about the simulator used, supported by citation.

claim: A series of 1000 stimuli were applied for each new parameter set to approach the simulator's steady state.
source: To approach the simulator's steady state, a series of 1000 stimuli were applied for each new parameter set starting from the initial states specified in the CellML file (when 1000 additional stimuli were applied, the maximum intracellular [Ca2+], [Cl-], and [Na+] changed by 1.5%, 0.15%, and 1.7%, respectively).
evidence: Methodological detail with data showing convergence.

claim: Sobol' sequences were used to generate 40,000 maximum conductance samples for training data.
source: Sobol' sequences were used to generate 40,000 maximum conductance samples, containing 20,000 maximum conductance samples between 0% and 200% of the original values and 20,000 maximum conductance samples between 50% and 150% of the original values.
evidence: Methodological detail about data generation.

claim: 20% of the initial training data set were randomly chosen for validation, leaving 31908 pairs for training.
source: From the initial training data set, 20% were randomly chosen to be used for validation leaving 31908 pairs of maximum conductances and corresponding APs for training.
evidence: Specific data about train-validation split.

claim: The emulator inputs were selected as GNa, GNaL, PCa, Gto, GKr, GKs, GK1, GNCX, and PNaK.
source: These assumptions allowed us to focus on maximum conductances and we considered those as inputs which either the AP is sensitive to (GNa, GNaL, PCa, Gto, GKr, GK1, GNCX, PNaK) or which are related to common drug targets (GNa, GNaL, PCa, Gto, GKr, GKs, GK1; Crumb et al., 2016) leading to the following selection: GNa, GNaL, PCa, Gto, GKr, GKs, GK1, GNCX, and PNaK.
evidence: Methodological decision based on sensitivity analysis and citation.

claim: The neural network was trained for a total number of 5000 epochs using the ADAM algorithm.
source: The neural network was trained for a total number of 5000 epochs using the first-order gradient-based algorithm ADAM Kingma and Ba, 2017.
evidence: Training methodology with citation.

claim: The simulation of a single action potential sampled at 20 kHz took 293 seconds on one core of an AMD Ryzen Threadripper 2990 WX in CARPentry.
source: The simulation of a single AP (see Simulator) sampled at a resolution of 20 kHZ took 293 s on one core of a AMD Ryzen Threadripper 2990 WX (clock rate: 3.0 GHZ) in CARPentry.
evidence: Measured computational performance data.

claim: Adaptive timestep solvers can significantly lower the simulation time to 30 seconds.
source: Adaptive timestep solver of variable order, such as implemented in Myokit (Clerx et al., 2016), can significantly lower the simulation time (30 s for our setup) by using small step sizes close to the depolarization (phase 0) and increasing the time step in all other phases.
evidence: Measured computational performance data with citation.

claim: Data set #2 consisted of 100 control data pairs and 10,000 drug data pairs with no samples excluded.
source: No sample was excluded and thus, the data set consisted of 100 control data pairs and 10,000 drug data pairs.
evidence: Specific data about the synthetic test dataset.

claim: Experimental action potentials were recorded in small right ventricular trabeculae and papillary tissue preparations isolated from healthy human hearts.
source: In the experimental data set, APs were recorded in small right ventricular trabeculae and papillary tissue preparations that were isolated from healthy human hearts (Orvos, 2019).
evidence: Description of experimental data source with citation.

claim: The hearts were obtained from organ donors whose hearts were explanted to obtain pulmonary and aortic valves for transplant surgery.
source: The hearts were obtained from organ donors whose hearts were explanted to obtain pulmonary and aortic valves for transplant surgery.
evidence: Description of experimental tissue source.

claim: All experimental measurements were performed at 37°C.
source: The conventional microelectrode technique was used for AP recordings and all measurements were carried out at 37°C.
evidence: Experimental condition specification.

claim: Seven experimental data pairs were excluded because biomarker values were not in the range found in the training data.
source: Pairs were excluded if the biomarker values (see AP biomarkers and abnormalities) of the control or the drugged AP were not in the range found in the training data (see Training). This applied to seven pairs and the final data set contained three pairs for cisapride, dofetilide, sotalol, and terfenadine, and one pair for verapamil.
evidence: Data exclusion criteria and resulting dataset composition.

claim: The final experimental data set contained three pairs for cisapride, dofetilide, sotalol, and terfenadine, and one pair for verapamil.
source: Pairs were excluded if the biomarker values (see AP biomarkers and abnormalities) of the control or the drugged AP were not in the range found in the training data (see Training). This applied to seven pairs and the final data set contained three pairs for cisapride, dofetilide, sotalol, and terfenadine, and one pair for verapamil.
evidence: Specific data about final experimental dataset composition.

claim: The average RMSE over all normal action potentials in data set #2 was 0.47 mV.
source: The average RMSE over all APs was 0.47 mV and only for a few APs the RMSE was >1 mV with 1.5 mV being the maximum.
evidence: Quantitative result from forward problem evaluation shown in Figure 5.

claim: The maximum RMSE for normal action potentials in data set #2 was 1.5 mV.
source: The average RMSE over all APs was 0.47 mV and only for a few APs the RMSE was >1 mV with 1.5 mV being the maximum.
evidence: Quantitative result from forward problem evaluation shown in Figure 5.

claim: 104 action potentials from data set #2 were emulated in 0.6 seconds.
source: In total 104 APs were emulated in 0.6 s.
evidence: Measured computational performance for forward problem.

claim: The emulator achieved 72.5% sensitivity in detecting early afterdepolarizations.
source: The emulations achieved 72.5% sensitivity (EAD cases correctly classified) and 94.9% specificity (non-EAD cases correctly classified), with an overall acurracy of 90.8% (total samples correctly classified).
evidence: Quantitative classification performance metrics.

claim: The emulator achieved 94.9% specificity in detecting early afterdepolarizations.
source: The emulations achieved 72.5% sensitivity (EAD cases correctly classified) and 94.9% specificity (non-EAD cases correctly classified), with an overall acurracy of 90.8% (total samples correctly classified).
evidence: Quantitative classification performance metrics.

claim: The emulator achieved 90.8% overall accuracy in classifying early afterdepolarizations.
source: The emulations achieved 72.5% sensitivity (EAD cases correctly classified) and 94.9% specificity (non-EAD cases correctly classified), with an overall acurracy of 90.8% (total samples correctly classified).
evidence: Quantitative classification performance metrics.

claim: The average RMSE over all EAD action potentials was 14.5 mV with 37.1 mV being the maximum.
source: The average RMSE over all EAD APs was 14.5 mV with 37.1 mV being the maximum.
evidence: Quantitative result from forward problem evaluation on EAD APs shown in Figure 7.

claim: The emulation of all 950 action potentials in data set #3 took 0.76 seconds on GPU.
source: The emulation of all 950 APs took 0.76 s on the GPU specified in Training
evidence: Measured computational performance for EAD dataset.

claim: Control and drugged action potentials in the inverse problem on synthetic data could be fitted with an average RMSE of 0.8 mV.
source: Control and drugged APs could be fitted with an average RMSE of 0.8 mV.
evidence: Quantitative result from inverse problem evaluation on synthetic data.

claim: The inverse problem on synthetic data required 10^8 emulations taking approximately 3.5 hours on GPU.
source: For this, we minimized (3) by using ADAM (Kingma and Ba, 2017) with no batching for 104 iterations for all 100 cardiomyocytes times 100 drugs (i.e. 104 APs), resulting in a total of 108 emulations, taking approximately 3.5 h on the GPU specified in Training.
evidence: Measured computational performance for inverse problem.

claim: The smallest RMSE in estimated pharmacological parameters was found for GKr.
source: However, the RMSEs increased from the control maximum conductance over the drugged maximum conductance to the pharmacological parameters and there were distinctive differences among maximum conductances and related pharmacological parameters with the smallest for GKr and the largest for GKs.
evidence: Comparative result from inverse problem evaluation shown in Figure 8.

claim: The largest RMSE in estimated pharmacological parameters was found for GKs.
source: However, the RMSEs increased from the control maximum conductance over the drugged maximum conductance to the pharmacological parameters and there were distinctive differences among maximum conductances and related pharmacological parameters with the smallest for GKr and the largest for GKs.
evidence: Comparative result from inverse problem evaluation shown in Figure 8.

claim: The total computational time for the inverse problem on experimental data was 2.8 hours on GPU.
source: The total computational time spent on this task was 2.8 hr on the GPU specified in Training.
evidence: Measured computational performance for inverse problem on experimental data.

claim: 50% of the pharmacological parameters estimated from experimental data could be successfully estimated when compared to CiPA distributions.
source: In total, 50% of the pharmacological parameters could be estimated succesfully and while all pharmacological parameters related to GKs could be successfully estimated, unsuccessfully estimated parameters were found across all maximum conductances, in particular related to GK1 for which all pharmacological parameters could not be successfully estimated (Table 5).
evidence: Quantitative result from inverse problem evaluation on experimental data shown in Figure 10 and Table 5.

claim: All pharmacological parameters related to GKs estimated from experimental data were successfully estimated.
source: In total, 50% of the pharmacological parameters could be estimated succesfully and while all pharmacological parameters related to GKs could be successfully estimated, unsuccessfully estimated parameters were found across all maximum conductances, in particular related to GK1 for which all pharmacological parameters could not be successfully estimated (Table 5).
evidence: Specific result from inverse problem evaluation on experimental data shown in Table 5.

claim: All pharmacological parameters related to GK1 estimated from experimental data could not be successfully estimated.
source: In total, 50% of the pharmacological parameters could be estimated succesfully and while all pharmacological parameters related to GKs could be successfully estimated, unsuccessfully estimated parameters were found across all maximum conductances, in particular related to GK1 for which all pharmacological parameters could not be successfully estimated (Table 5).
evidence: Specific result from inverse problem evaluation on experimental data shown in Table 5.

claim: The NN emulator demonstrates the capability of accounting for discontinuities, a major advantage over existing emulation strategies.
source: This demonstrates not only very fast and mostly very accurate AP emulations but also the capability of accounting for discontinuities, a major advantage over existing emulation strategies.
evidence: Inference drawn from the EAD emulation results.

claim: Inaccuracies in estimating pharmacological parameters from experimental data can be attributed to the fact that small tissue preparations were studied while the emulator was trained on single cardiomyocyte data.
source: However, notable mismatches were observed between pharmacological parameters estimated from experimental data and distributions obtained from the Comprehensive in vitro Proarrhythmia Assay initiative. This reveals larger inaccuracies which can be attributed particularly to the fact that small tissue preparations were studied while the emulator was trained on single cardiomyocyte data.
evidence: Inference about source of error based on methodological differences.

claim: Action potentials in small tissue preparations are slightly different from those in single cardiomyocytes.
source: The second and probably main reason for the inaccuracies may be the fact that the data were collected in small tissue preparations, whereas the emulator was trained on data generated by a simulator that represents single cardiomyocytes. APs in small tissue preparations are slightly different from those in single cardiomyocytes.
evidence: Statement based on established knowledge about tissue vs. single cell electrophysiology.

claim: Differences between tissue and single cell action potentials can arise from electrotonic coupling and the mixture of cells including fibroblasts.
source: Differences can arise from electrotonic coupling and the mixture of cells including fibroblasts that are able to modify the EP (Kohl and Gourdie, 2014; Mayer et al., 2017; Hall et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to relevant literature.

claim: The emulator enables massive speed-ups compared to regular simulations.
source: The presented NN emulator enables a massive speed-up compared to regular simulations and the evaluation for the forward problem on synthetic data showed also highly accurate AP emulations.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from computational performance measurements.

claim: The continuous nature of the emulator allows the action potential to be emulated and fitted at any desired resolution.
source: In addition to the aforementioned strengths of the presented NN emulator, some further valuable features are worth mentioning that arise from the continuous nature of the emulator. First, the AP can be emulated and fitted at any desired resolution.
evidence: Inference about capability based on emulator architecture.

claim: Timing offsets can be accounted for using t₀ in the optimization without retraining the emulator.
source: Second, timing offsets, for example between stimuli in the data to be fitted and the training data, can be accounted for using t0 in (3) without retraining.
evidence: Inference about capability based on emulator architecture and optimization formulation.

claim: The emulator has only maximum conductances as inputs, which is a limitation.
source: Some limitations have to be considered. First, the emulator has only maximum conductances as inputs.
evidence: Acknowledged limitation of the study design.

claim: Maximum conductances explain much of the action potential variability seen between cardiomyocytes.
source: Although these explain much of the AP variability seen between cardiomyocytes (Britton et al., 2013; Muszkiewicz et al., 2016), the inclusion of parameters related to the channel kinetics might enable a more detailed consideration of drug effects in pharmacological studies.
evidence: Supported by citations to relevant literature.

claim: The interaction between drugs and their targets is solely captured through scaling of the related maximum conductance at control, which is an oversimplification.
source: Second, the interaction between drugs and their targets is solely captured through scaling of the related maximum conductance at control, which is mostly adequate but in fact an oversimplification (Brennan et al., 2009).
evidence: Acknowledged limitation with citation.

claim: The inverse problem was only solved for action potential data obtained from one single stimulation protocol.
source: Third, the inverse problem was only solved for AP data obtained from one single stimulation protocol.
evidence: Acknowledged limitation of the study design.

claim: Johnstone et al., 2016 showed that the usage of action potential data obtained from various stimulation protocols can improve parameter identifiability.
source: Johnstone et al., 2016 have shown that the usage of AP data obtained from various stimulation protocols can improve the parameter identifiability and thus, the accuracy of parameter estimates.
evidence: Supported by citation to relevant literature.

claim: The number of drugs and concentrations considered in the inverse problem on experimental data poses a limitation.
source: Last but not least, the number of drugs and concentrations considered in the inverse problem on experimental data poses a limitation.
evidence: Acknowledged limitation of the study scope.

claim: The presented approach can be straightforwardly applied to other transients such as intracellular [Ca2+] or sarcomere length.
source: Of note, the presented approach can also be straightforwardly applied to other transients, for example intracellular [Ca2+] or sarcomere length.
evidence: Speculation about potential extensions of the method.

claim: The computational cost of the NN emulator revealed a massive speed-up of more than 1e3 compared to the simulator.
source: The computational cost of the NN emulator was compared to that of the simulator, revealing a massive speed-up of more than 1e3.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from computational performance measurements.

claim: The accuracy of solving the forward problem on synthetic data was found to be high for normal action potentials.
source: The accuracy of solving the forward problem on synthetic data was found to be high for normal APs and this hold mostly true for abnormal APs exhibiting EADs.
evidence: Summary of results from forward problem evaluation.

claim: The accuracy of solving the forward problem on synthetic data held mostly true for abnormal action potentials exhibiting early afterdepolarizations.
source: The accuracy of solving the forward problem on synthetic data was found to be high for normal APs and this hold mostly true for abnormal APs exhibiting EADs.
evidence: Summary of results from forward problem evaluation.

claim: The accuracy of solving the inverse problem on synthetic data remained high.
source: While larger inaccuracies were observed when utilizing experimental data – a limitation thoroughly discussed and particularly inherent to the fact that small tissue preparations were studied while the emulator was trained on single cardiomyocyte data – the accuracy of solving the inverse problem on synthetic data remained high.
evidence: Summary of results from inverse problem evaluation.

claim: These findings underscore the potential of NN emulators in improving the efficiency of future quantitative systems pharmacology studies.
source: Collectively, these findings underscore the potential of NN emulators in improving the efficiency of future quantitative systems pharmacology studies.
evidence: Overall conclusion drawn from all results.
